 Taipei, Oct. 24 (CNA) The land warning for Typhoon Champi is expected to be lifted Saturday evening as the storm moves away from Taiwan, according to the Central Weather Administration (CWA).
 Speaking to reporters, Wu Wan-hua (伍婉華), deputy director of the CWA's Weather Forecast Center, said Champi was likely to weaken into a tropical storm Saturday afternoon. The sea warning for the storm was expected to be lifted Saturday night, she said.
 The CWA issued a sea warning for Champi late Wednesday and a land warning Thursday morning.
 As the storm weakened, its radius shrank to 250 kilometers from 280 km over the past few hours, while its accompanying cloud system became more scattered, Wu said.
 Rainfall brought by the storm would continue to ease Saturday morning, she added.
 As of 10 a.m. Saturday, Champi was centered at about 170 km east-northeast of Yilan County in northeastern Taiwan, moving north at 21 kph, according to CWA data.
 The typhoon had maximum sustained winds of 126 kph, gusts of up to 162 kph, the data shows.
 According to the Central Emergency Operations Center (CEOC), the strong winds and heavy rains of Champi had left one person dead and 527 injured in Taiwan as of Saturday morning.
 The death was reported in Liuqiu Township, Pingtung County, where a man was swept away by storm-driven waves on a beach Thursday, and the injuries mostly occurred in Taipei and Taichung cities, the CEOC said.
 The CEOC added the injuries were largely caused by downed trees, falling electricity cables and billboards and damaged water pipes.
 Although the worst of the typhoon's impact was over, windward areas in western Taiwan were still experiencing heavy rain, particularly in mountainous areas of Miaoli County in northern Taiwan, Wu said.
 An extremely heavy rain advisory or a heavy rain advisory was in effect for mountainous areas of Taipei, New Taipei and Taoyuan cities, as well as Hsinchu and Miaoli counties in northern Taiwan.
 A heavy rain advisory was also in effect for Keelung and the north coast, Taipei, New Taipei and Taoyuan cities, Hsinchu City, Hsinchu and Miaoli counties, Taichung City and Nantou County in central Taiwan, mountainous areas of Yunlin, Chiayi and Pingtung counties and Kaohsiung and Tainan cities in southern Taiwan, as well as Yilan County.
 An extremely heavy rain advisory means rainfall is expected to exceed 200 mm in 24 hours or 100 mm in three hours, while a heavy rain advisory means rainfall is expected to exceed 80 mm in 24 hours or 40 mm in one hour, according to the CWA.
 Rain is expected to taper off from Saturday night through early Sunday morning, with precipitation likely to gradually stop in southern, southeastern and eastern Taiwan on Sunday morning.
 Winds triggered by Champi are also expected to weaken. Late Friday night, Sandiao Cape in New Taipei, Taiwan's easternmost point, recorded a gust exceeding 221 kph, she said.
 Despite Champi's weakening, waves generated by the storm remained high, particularly in waters north and east of Taiwan, where waves exceeding six meters were reported, Wu said.
 (By Huang Chiao-wen, Liu Chien-pang and Frances Huang)
